source: MAFF/GIZ, "Guidelines for Banana Export from Cambodia to China" (2022), section 5.4
text:
For orchards supplying export banana, field sanitation is treated as a formal requirement rather than just good practice: fields need to be kept clear of fallen/rotting fruit and plant debris that can harbor pests or disease, weeds around the growing area need to be controlled, and irrigation water sources should be free of contamination. Companies exporting to China are expected to enforce this discipline consistently across all the farms/plots supplying them, since a single contaminated or poorly maintained plot in a supply chain can jeopardize the traceability and clean-status claims made for an entire shipment.

For a smallholder farmer supplying an export-oriented company under contract, this means field sanitation practices that support disease and pest control generally (see the field-level pest and disease entries elsewhere in this knowledge base) are not optional extras but a condition of staying in the export supply chain.
